public_rationale: Marcus forecast that 2025 agent demos would not work very reliably. Independent 2025 benchmarks back this. On CMU's TheAgentCompany, the best agent finished only 30% of realistic workplace tasks. On Salesforce's CRMArena-Pro, leading agents managed about 58% on single-turn business tasks and about 35% on multi-turn ones. In late 2025, Anthropic's best computer-use agent scored 61.4% on OSWorld, so it still failed about 4 in 10 tasks. Coding agents did better, at about 77% on SWE-bench Verified. Even so, they failed nearly a quarter of tasks, and progress during the year was fast. Under the plain reading, 2025 agents were not reliable. The forecast holds.
limitations: There is no numeric threshold, so the result depends on reading 'not all that reliably' as a large share of failures.
The evidence is mostly benchmarks, not field failure rates.
Coding agents were notably more capable than general agents, and products were more than mere demos. That part of the post is not scored here.

from_speaker: All that we will have this year are demos
those demos won't work all that reliably
our_interpretation: Plain reading: AI agents released or shown in 2025 would fail a large share of realistic multi-step tasks, falling well short of the near-perfect reliability needed to trust them without supervision.
Independent or academic benchmarks of realistic agent tasks published in 2025 are the right test. Top-agent success rates well below 90% on such tasks count as 'not all that reliable'.
This assessment does not test whether 'all we will have are demos'. It tests only the reliability part.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations published in 2025 show leading agents failing a substantial share (for example, a third or more) of realistic multi-step tasks, or documented live deployments show frequent errors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations published in 2025 show leading agents completing realistic, varied multi-step tasks with high reliability (for example, above about 90%) across the board.

evidence.excerpt: find that the most competitive agent can complete 30% of tasks autonomously.
evidence.explanation: In the 2025 revision, the best agent finished only 30% of realistic workplace tasks on its own. That is far from reliable.

evidence.excerpt: leading LLM agents achieve only around 58% single-turn success on CRMArena-Pro, with performance dropping significantly to approximately 35% in multi-turn settings.
evidence.explanation: Leading agents failed about 42% of single-turn and about 65% of multi-turn business tasks in mid-2025.

evidence.excerpt: On OSWorld, a benchmark that tests AI models on real-world computer tasks, Sonnet 4.5 now leads at 61.4%. Just four months ago, Sonnet 4 held the lead at 42.2%.
evidence.explanation: Even the leading computer-use agent of late 2025 failed about 39% of real-world computer tasks. Progress was fast, but reliability was still limited.

evidence.excerpt: We report 77.2%, which was averaged over 10 trials, no test-time compute, and 200K thinking budget on the full 500-problem SWE-bench Verified dataset.
evidence.explanation: Coding agents reached about 77% on a well-defined coding benchmark. This is the strongest 2025 counterpoint, though they still failed nearly a quarter of tasks.
